RULE 1 (first-of-repeated) — line 40: isArray(value) ? value[0] : value, with occurrence-order arrays proven above; repeated key's cap position is its FIRST occurrence (indexOf de-dupe, lines 73-75). A repeated param whose first occurrence is valueless yields null (e.g. '?utm_x&utm_x=a' → [null,'a'] → null) — first-occurrence semantics honored.

RULE 2 AS AMENDED (surrogate-safe truncation) — lines 42-47: .slice(0, 255) (TRACKING_VALUE_MAX_LENGTH = 255, line 36), then charCodeAt(length-1) checked against 0xd800–0xdbff and dropped via slice(0, -1) → 254 code units. Spec→code: a pair-splitting slice always leaves a trailing HIGH surrogate; the code drops exactly that range. Code→spec: the check is textually unconditional (fires also on a value ALREADY ending in a lone high surrogate with no slice split), but that input is unreachable through the contract — location.search is a USVString (no raw unpaired surrogates), and decode-uri-component v0.2.0 cannot emit a lone surrogate (decodeURIComponent throws on surrogate-codepoint UTF-8 like %ED%A0%80; the fallback substitutes only valid decodings, U+FFFD, or literal percent text — verified in its installed source). Trailing unpaired LOW surrogate is likewise unreachable: pre-slice values contain surrogates only as proper pairs, and a low surrogate at the slice's last index has its high partner at index 253 (still paired). So the amended invariant 'a value must never end in an unpaired surrogate' is fully enforced for every contract-reachable input, and the amended §5.1 rule 2 / §7 constraint 1 / §11 note 4 texts describe the shipped behavior accurately and completely.
